title: Absolute second-increment heat-kernel bound via flow-Jacobian cancellation for stable SDEs
difficulty_reason: Even after the old two-sided parametrix and q estimates are allowed, the absolute second-increment integral requires a new endpoint cancellation. The authors integrate the frozen density over its terminal variable, subtract its unit mass after a flow change of variables and retain the Jacobian defect to gain the gamma and alpha+beta-1 time powers. They then isolate this integrated defect at the flow centre, pair the other early-time term with a spatial Holder difference of q, and close the late-time part with a separate convolution bound. This mass-defect construction and singular-integral closure are not delivered by the previously selected two-sided bound.
